definition: The simplified sequential decision problem of choosing among options with unknown rewards, balancing exploration and exploitation without full state dynamics.
details: The simplified sequential decision problem of choosing among options with unknown rewards, balancing exploration and exploitation without full state dynamics.

explainer.lead: Multi-armed bandits is the simplified sequential decision problem of choosing among options with unknown rewards while balancing exploration and exploitation. It matters because it isolates that trade-off without full state dynamics.

tiers.eli5: You face a set of choices whose payoffs you don't know yet, and each pick teaches you something while possibly earning something. The trick is deciding when to try something new and when to keep using what works.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use this simplified framing to study and tune exploration versus exploitation without modeling full state dynamics. The simplification is the point: it strips the problem to option choice under unknown rewards.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as the simplified sequential decision problem of choosing among options with unknown rewards, balancing exploration and exploitation without full state dynamics.

explainer.example: An agent picks among options with unknown rewards, trading off trying untested options against reusing the one that has paid off so far.
